prompt: The growing number of overweight people is putting a strain on the health care system in an effort to deal with the health issues involved. Some people think that the best way to deal with this problem is to introduce more physical education lessons in the school curriculum. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
The escalating number of obese individuals burdening the healthcare system in an effort to deal with the health complications involved has become a controversial topic. Many people argue that introducing more physical education lessons in the school curriculum is the best way to solve the problem, while others hold opposing views. As far as I am concerned, I strongly disagree with the former claim. This essay will present my viewpoint and opinions.

To begin with, I believe that implementing more physical education classes in the education system will not automatically lead to a decline in the population's obesity rate, since external factors such as diet and daily routines will not be taken into account. For example, although students may engage in higher levels of physical activity at school, their unhealthy eating habits outside school may remain unchanged. Moreover, obesity can be a hereditary trait, which means that some aspects are fundamentally unalterable due to genetics.

Furthermore, whether students are physically active beyond the classroom is outside the school's control. Since students come from different families with varying lifestyles, there is no guarantee that all of them will adopt habits that are beneficial for their health. With that said, fully addressing the issue of obesity requires utmost cooperation between educational institutions, families, and healthcare providers.

Additionally, physical education lessons may not be effective for every student, as a minority may have medical conditions, such as asthma, that limit their ability to participate in high-impact exercises. Therefore, simply increasing the amount of time allocated to physical education lessons will not ensure that students develop health-conscious habits in the long run.

To summarize, I reject the idea that increasing the number of physical education lessons is the most effective way to tackle obesity, as unhealthy dietary patterns, lifestyles, and biological factors also play significant roles in this issue.
